html:
SMTO-GWT-0048 — SMTO couldn't confirm that a Gateway restarted

GUID: 16bbb5dc-4a18-4138-887c-a05db1e4715e
Slug: gateway-restart-response-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO asked a Gateway (the helper program that runs work on another computer) to restart, but its reply was missing or unreadable. It may be restarting now, or it may never have received the request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait about a minute, then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that Gateway. A restarting Gateway goes offline for a moment and then comes back, so a fresh check shows where it is now.
  2. Select the Gateway's name to expand it. If it is marked Outbound, a Last connected time after your restart request means it already restarted. An Outbound Gateway reconnects to SMTO each time it starts, so that time shows the restart happened.
  3. Otherwise, ask the person who manages that Gateway computer to check when the Gateway program last started. The missing reply doesn't tell SMTO whether the restart happened, but the Gateway computer itself knows.
  4. Only if the Gateway clearly did not restart and isn't busy, ask for the restart again the same way you did before. Sending a second restart while the first is under way can interrupt the Gateway again.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows the Gateway as Connected, and you know whether the first restart already happened.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. If the Gateway stays offline, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer so they can check it there. Don't send several restart requests in a row.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway restart request returned undecodable JSON, a non-object body, an unrecognized status or an unexpected transport exception, so no valid restart acknowledgement was received.

What this means

  • Restart transport returned undecodable JSON, a non-object body, an unrecognized status or an unexpected exception. No valid acknowledgment establishes whether restart was scheduled or occurred. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Restart transport returned undecodable JSON, a non-object body, an unrecognized status or an unexpected exception. No valid acknowledgment establishes whether restart was scheduled or occurred.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the recorded restart attempt, current Gateway health and retained active work before considering another request.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway's health (Check connection in Settings › Setup › Gateways, or the Gateway health API) together with its own log or process start time; for an Outbound Gateway, a last_connected_at after the request also shows a restart. Confirm no execution is still draining. A lost acknowledgement does not establish whether restart occurred; send another restart request only after health shows it did not.
  • Inspect Gateway health and active work before requesting another restart. A lost acknowledgement does not establish whether restart occurred.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The Gateway's restart and readiness state is established without duplicating an uncertain restart request.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
